title: timeout-root-cause-hypothesis-board
body:
Purpose: propose a hypothesis-driven investigation board (H-Board) for the Console that makes triage of timeouts and 5xx model/service errors faster and more measurable. This doc focuses on UX scaffolding, minimal data surface, and a short backlog for an MVP.

Key idea: instead of surfacing raw traces + logs only, present a small set of structured hypotheses (root-cause guesses) for each incident, each paired with evidence and a one-click test action. Investigators can rank hypotheses, attach outcomes, and mark remediation steps. Over time captured outcomes feed back into automated hypothesis suggestions.

Why: current flows dump a ton of telemetry and force engineers to mentally map signals to causes. The H-Board reduces cognitive load, makes decisions auditable, and helps capture operational knowledge for retraining routing/fallback policies and for Improve/Optimize features.

Users and personas:
- On-call SRE: needs fast, high-confidence ways to decide rollback/fallback and estimate MTTR.
- Platform engineer on-call: wants reproducible repro steps and safe test knobs (traffic reroute, small replays).
- Engineer owning routing/model: needs evidence to triage whether model variant or network/hardware issue.
- Support/CS triage: needs concise summary and remediation ETA to inform customers.

Primary scenarios:
1) Spike in request timeouts for a model route: H-Board surfaces 3 suggested hypotheses: (A) downstream model queue saturation, (B) GPU OOM/driver transient, (C) network egress throttling. Each hypothesis lists supporting signals (p99 latency, GPU mem pressure, trace spans showing connection resets) and offers test actions (replay with lower concurrency, switch to compatible model variant, reroute to a different region).
2) Intermittent 5xx for inference calls: board shows candidate causes including model decode errors, tokenizer mismatch, or input size overflow. Evidence thumbnails include sample request payloads that triggered 5xx and sample model logs.
3) Cross-correlation: the board can surface related incidents (same model, same region) and suggest a combined hypothesis.

Success metrics (MVP):
- Mean time to first actionable hypothesis reduced by 40% in post-mortem trials.
- Fraction of incidents with recorded hypothesis outcomes > 60% in first 90 days.
- Investigator satisfaction score (survey) +15 points vs current flow.

Design constraints and principles:
- Minimal surface area for MVP: show at most 4 hypotheses by default.
- Prefer evidence thumbnails over raw logs; link to full logs/traces.
- Keep actions safe and auditable: any automated test that mutates routing requires confirmation and audit log entry.
- Avoid funneling new users to complex UIs; provide an optional "guided triage" experience.

MVP wireframe description (high level):
- Header: incident summary (route, model, region, incident window, total failures/timeouts). Quick actions: acknowledge, mute, escalate.
- Hypothesis lanes (stacked vertically): each lane card contains hypothesis title, confidence slider (auto-suggested), short explanation, 2–3 evidence bullets (with micro-thumbnails), one primary test action button, and an outcome dropdown (resolved/invalid/needs follow-up).
- Evidence thumbnails: short visualizations (p99 latency sparkline, small trace snapshot, sample request payload snippet, GPU mem gauge). Clicking expands to full trace/log in side panel.
- Test sandbox modal: lightweight UI to re-run a sample request with toggles: model variant, token limit, reduced concurrency, region override. Test runs in an isolated replay sandbox and outputs head/tail tokens + latency + error code. Each run stored as a timestamped artifact.
- Timeline and audit trail: linear timeline below hypotheses showing hypothesis creation, tests run, outcome changes, owner comments, and remediation steps. Timeline entries can be collapsed into activity groups.
- Outcomes dashboard: aggregate view for reliability team showing hypothesis accuracy over time (helpful to tune automated suggestion engine).

Unique UX patterns (differentiators):
- Confidence slider: investigators can indicate confidence (0–100%) when creating or endorsing a hypothesis; the system tracks calibration.
- Hypothesis templates: prefilled cards based on common patterns (queue saturation, model OOM, tokenizer error, input overflow, auth/quotas). Templates include suggested evidence queries and tests.
- Evidence rollups: combine multiple micro-evidence into a single digest (e.g., 4 traces collapsed into "connection resets observed on 12/12 across nodes 3/5").
- Outcome tagging for ML regressions: if outcome marked "model regression" board captures the request set for a small eval run and links to Evaluate/Optimize pipelines.

Data required for MVP (minimal):
- Per-request metadata: route, model version, region, request id, timestamps, error code.
- Aggregates: p50/p90/p99 latency, error counts by code, concurrency metrics.
- Traces: sampled trace spans with span names and errors.
- Runtime metrics: GPU memory and utilization per worker, queue lengths, restart events.
- Sample request payloads (redacted PII) for failing calls.

Privacy and security notes:
- Sample payloads must be redacted before display; default to stored ephemeral artifacts with TTL 30 days.
- Automated tests in sandbox must not route live customer traffic; always run replays against a sandboxed capacity or allow a small percentage of mirrored traffic only with explicit permission.

Operational considerations:
- Audit log for every hypothesis action (create/edit/test/outcome) with user, time, and optional comment.
- RBAC: only SRE and platform engineers can run destructive tests (e.g., routing changes). Product/CS can run read-only replays.
- Storage: store test runs and short artifacts for 90 days by default to enable post-incident learning.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: over-reliance on suggested hypotheses could bias investigators. Mitigation: show source signals and allow full access to raw telemetry. Include a "challenge this suggestion" button that nudges user to provide counter-evidence.
- Risk: expensive replays run at scale. Mitigation: limit concurrency and total token budget per replay, surface estimated cost before run.

Open questions to resolve in grooming:
- How to prioritize which hypotheses are auto-suggested and how to surface confidence? (ML classifier vs rule-based heuristics)
- TTLs for artifacts and retention policy for sample payloads.
- Integration surface with Evaluate/Optimize for outcomes marked as model regressions.
mockup_notes:
Sketch A (single incident view): header + two columns. Left column: Hypothesis lanes stacked (4 max). Right column: Evidence panel with expanded trace/log viewer and test sandbox CTA. Timeline at bottom.

Sketch B (compact summary for paging in incidents list): show top hypothesis + confidence sparkline + 1-line primary evidence + quick test icon that opens sandbox.

Visual affordances: color-code hypothesis cards by suggested action (yellow = investigate, orange = test-run suggested, red = escalate/rollback candidate). Use thin sparklines for latency and small status badges for model/worker health.

Accessibility: keyboard-first flows for running a test, clear labels on confidence slider, tooltips for evidence thumbnails, and high-contrast colors for statuses.
backlog_items: H-001: Backend API: hypothesis CRUD and outcome audit (2 wks)
H-002: Ingest hook: sample-request redaction + artifact store (1 wk)
H-003: Frontend: hypothesis lanes + evidence panel (3 wks)
H-004: Replay sandbox: safe re-run infra + cost guardrails (3 wks)
H-005: Auto-suggest rules: rule-based initial engine (1 wk)
H-006: RBAC and audit logs integration with SSO (1 wk)
H-007: Metrics events: hypothesis acted-on, test-runed, outcome set (0.5 wk)
H-008: Post-MVP: ML-based hypothesis ranking pipeline (3–4 wks)
H-009: Integrate "model regression" outcome with Evaluate/Optimize (2 wks)
H-010: UX polish: templates, keyboard shortcuts, accessibility fixes (1–2 wks)
acceptance_criteria: Create hypothesis flow: user can create a hypothesis, attach evidence links, and set initial confidence
Test action: user can run a sandboxed replay that records latency and error outcome without impacting live traffic
Outcome recording: users can set outcome and add comments; each change is auditable
Evidence linking: thumbnails link to full trace/log panel
RBAC: only authorized roles can run routing-changing tests
Retention: artifacts created by tests have TTL and admin-configurable retention
grooming_notes:
Grooming session 2025-02-20 notes: team agreed MVP should prioritize safe replays and basic templates. MVP will be feature-flagged for a subset of customers and SREs for 6 weeks. Estimated total effort for MVP (backend + frontend + infra) = 9–10 developer-weeks. Prioritize H-001, H-004, H-002, H-003 in sprint planning.

Action items assigned:
- Miguel: prototype replay-sandbox gating and cost estimator (due 2025-02-28).
- Sofia: redact policy and artifact storage spec (due 2025-03-04).
- Tom: wireframe interactive prototype (Figma) and keyboard flows (due 2025-02-26).

Notes from SRE: keep default suggested hypotheses conservative and surface clear confidence signals. We should instrument hypothesis accuracy metric from day one.

Next grooming checklist: finalize evidence schema, define replay budget defaults, finalize RBAC mapping, add telemetry events for ML training.
